newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SPC 1st-half net set to double - analysts.
newsitem.headline: SPC 1st-half net set to double - analysts.

text.p: Singapore Petroleum Co Ltd (SPC) is expected to report a doubling in its first half net earnings on Friday, analysts said.
SPC made a first-half net profit of Singapore $5.1 million in the six months to June 30, 1995.
Analysts said on Thursday their optimistic forecast was based on strong refining margins and record post-Gulf War prices for diesel and jet fuel in the first half of 1996.
Esso Malaysia Bhd reported a 28 percent rise in net profit to 37.91 million ringgit for the first half of 1996 while Shell Refining Co operating profit soared by 176 percent to 55.73 million ringgit.
"SPC's net profits should get a big boost from the high prices of jet fuel and diesel that were seen earlier this year," one analyst said.
Jet fuel prices in Singapore hit a five-year record of almost US$34.00 per barrel during peak winter demand in early January.
SPC has a 20 percent share of the 57,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) Singapore jet fuel market -- making it the largest supplier of jet fuel to Singapore's Changi airport, analysts said.

In a research report, securities firm DBS Investment Research Ltd said the start up of a new residue catalytic cracker, which converts fuel oil to gasoline, diesel and jet fuel, should also have boosted margins.
Singapore Refining Co (SRC), in which SPC has a one-third stake, started up a 33,000-bpd cracker last October.
SRC also raised its refining capacity by 60,000 bpd to 285,000 bpd last August.
